key_insight: A single-ancilla hybrid quantum–classical method reconstructs spin-system energy-level degeneracies and thermodynamic properties from partition-function measurements at imaginary inverse temperatures.
engineering_relevance: The approach offers a route to extracting thermodynamic observables on quantum hardware, with circuit optimizations that exploit commuting interactions and Eulerian ordering.
method: Use one ancilla qubit to measure the partition function at imaginary inverse temperatures.
Apply an inverse discrete Fourier transform to recover degeneracies on a known, equally spaced energy grid.
Optimize circuits using commuting interactions and Eulerian ordering.
evidence_signal: Tests on periodic Kagome Ising antiferromagnets with up to 36 spins using ibm_kingston retained dominant spectral features and reproduced the main temperature dependence of exact heat capacities despite hardware noise.
watch_item: Exact, leakage-free reconstruction assumes a known, equally spaced energy grid and noiseless measurements; deep circuits introduce hardware-noise sensitivity.
paper_title: Quantum computation of energy level degeneracy and thermodynamical properties of spin systems
